reason: Both give the right headline numbers (120.2 s with 66.3 s planner waiting vs 56.8 s with none, the instruction at 49.8 s arriving after Prague's last call began at 46.9 s), and A's prose and its seven-pattern table and caveats are the stronger written account. But A is a replay that cannot be watched at phone width: its chart box shows only about 0-40 s (0-22 s in scene 5) and does not follow the playhead (scrollLeft stayed at 0 throughout playback), so the waits after 40 s in scene 2, the end of the async run in scene 3, and the urgent report, the instruction and 'never read' in scene 5 all happen off-screen unless the reader swipes, and swiping hides the lane labels. B fits the full 0-120 s axis on a 390 px screen with sync, async and the progress-report run stacked on one shared time axis plus a timestamped event log, so the reader sees the hatched sync waits pile up while async finishes, and parts 7-8 mark '503', 'last call began 46.9 s' and 'reply never read' right on the Prague lane. Every number B shows matched facts.md, and its pause and timeline scrubber worked.

A: At 390 px (and still at 560 px) the timeline is clipped to roughly the first 20-40 s and never auto-scrolls with the playhead, so the key events of scenes 2, 3 and 5 (sync waits after 40 s, the late instruction at 49.8 s) play off-screen; swiping right also scrolls the lane labels away.

Scene 5 counts 'messages between agents so far: 10' for the progress-and-redirect run, while the recorded comparison table gives 6 messages for that level, and the count's definition is not explained.

Scene 4's 'where the time went' bar chart is also clipped at phone width (its title and dashed comparison bars run off the right edge), so the split of own work vs waiting cannot be read without swiping.
B: Lane labels, axis ticks and the faded comparison runs are small, low-contrast text on a dark background and are hard to read at phone width.
Never says that 'waited' counts only the planner, so a reader may not know that helpers also waited (for example the Rome helper's 10.8 s in another run).
Playback advances from part to part by itself and the dense one-line intro packs every result in before the replay starts; a reader who does not pause can miss a part's caption.
